Karansul

Overview

Karansul is an Ingos merchant angry that Yam-Akara’s cheap runes undercut his business. Later his private relationship with Geraldine becomes evidence in the murder inquiry: the two provide each other with an alibi and reveal plans to marry. His commercial grudges should not be mistaken for proof of murder. [1, 2]

Two magicians on Ingos

Kir and Kel seek magical help on Ingos. Karansul complains about Yam-Akara, whose cheap runes undercut his trade, and identifies His as the governor’s court magician. His receives the travellers with suspicion and later asks them to retrieve materials from his laboratory. Sver the Trapper offers another route: contact Grey Leaf through the Sacred Flower and a vessel from his cache. Grey Leaf explains that the knight Brissen and his magician friend have left for the settlement near the mines. Kir’s first task here is finding an informed ally, before the murder that later dominates the investigation. The vessel Sver asks them to carry is for Woodsfolk balm that eases his own aching joints. He has used their necessary visit to obtain a personal favour. [1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]

Grey Leaf and the poisoned river

Grey Leaf reports that animals are dying after drinking from the northern river. His healers cannot save them while Karansul’s factory keeps discharging poison into the water. Kel recognises that treating the animals alone cannot solve the problem. Karansul proudly confirms his ownership and describes a blasting powder used in his mines. Kir can obtain the powder and destroy the polluting works. Grey Leaf thanks him for ending the contamination. This request concerns the Woodsfolk’s protection of the forest, separately from the search for the Joon artifact. [9, 10, 11, 12]

Geraldine’s secret meetings

Trickster notices that Geraldine repeatedly leaves the settlement in secret. As its leader, he argues, she should not keep matters from her people. He asks Kir and Kel to follow her. They see a meeting with a man, but magical traps prevent them from approaching unnoticed and frighten the pair away. Their first report therefore establishes a secret meeting, not the man’s identity. Suspicion later falls on both His and Karansul; the eventual explanation is Geraldine’s relationship with the merchant, whom she plans to marry. [13, 14, 2]

The planted knife and His’s death

A knife found at the murder site appears to implicate His. The court magician admits it was stolen from his laboratory together with the governor’s nugget. He had sent out the empty caravan to hide that loss and hoped to blame raiders after an informant warned of the planned attack. His arranges a meeting to produce evidence, but is killed before he can clear himself. Meanwhile Geraldine and Karansul disclose their relationship and provide each other with an alibi. Their commercial hostility and private secrecy had made them suspicious without establishing guilt. [15, 16, 17, 18, 2]
